8.0 STORAGE, CATALOG AND THE NODE SERVICE

8.1 The folders are the truth

V1 keeps manifests: stored lists of what is in each folder, rebuilt at start-up and checked for missing files (P-10). In V2 the catalog is worked out from the folders and a small metadata file beside each item; nothing else is stored about them.

library/scripts/curve-stitch/manyRowsColumns.js          the item
library/scripts/curve-stitch/manyRowsColumns.meta.json   { "status": "favorite", "tags": [...], "order": 3, "hidden": false }
library/scripts/curve-stitch/manyRowsColumns.png         its thumbnail, made by the renderer
DR-8.1The catalog entry of an item shall be: its id (path from the library root, without extension), kind, category (its folder), title (from its header or meta), status and tags (from .meta.json), thumbnail, and for scripts the host's report (section 9). It is rebuilt for one item when that item's files change.
DR-8.2Renaming or moving an item shall be a command that moves its files, its metadata, its thumbnail and its journal together (FR-6.16.2).
DR-8.3Archiving shall move an item into its category's archive/ folder; archived items are left out of lists, tests and the catalog, and can be brought back.

8.2 The Node service

One process on one port (5174). Requests are POST /dispatch with { requestName, payload }, as in V1. The service also keeps one Server-Sent Events connection open to tell the application that files changed.

RequestPayloadReply
catalog.list{ kind?, category? }{ entries: CatalogEntry[] }
item.read{ id }{ text, meta }
item.write{ id, text, expectedVersion }{ version } or { conflict: currentVersion }
item.move{ id, toId }{ id }
item.archive{ id }{ archivedId }
meta.write{ id, meta }{}
thumbnail.write{ id, png (base64) }{}
journal.append{ id, entry }{}
journal.read{ id, since? }{ entries }
log.append{ kind: "errors" | ..., lines }{ name }
log.list / log.read{ limit } / { name }V1's listLogFiles / readLogFile
output.write{ id, format, bytes }{ path } (SVG, PDF, DXF beside the item)
editor.open{ id }opens the file in VS Code
history.vscode{ id }VS Code's saved versions (V1 Script history, kept as a bridge)
status{}{ version, root, uptime } (FR-6.18.6)
DR-8.4Every path in a payload shall be an id relative to the library root; the service resolves it and refuses anything outside the root, any .. segment, and any absolute path (V1's path-safety module, kept).
DR-8.5Every write shall go to a temporary file in the same folder and be renamed into place, so a crash leaves the old file whole (V1 already does this for figures).
DR-8.6item.write takes the version the editor read; if the file has changed since (the owner edited it in VS Code), the write is refused with the current version, and the application offers to reload or keep both.
DR-8.7The service shall accept requests only from the application's own origin and from no origin (local tools), and refuse other origins and hosts (V1's rule).
DR-8.8The file watcher shall debounce changes by 200 ms and report { id, change: "added" | "changed" | "removed" }; a new item appears within 2 s (FR-6.9.2).
DR-8.9When the service does not answer, the application shall say so in the status strip and go read-only: every command that writes is greyed with "the Node service is not running (start it with ...)" (FR-6.18.6).
[[FIG dynamic_add | Adding an item by saving a file]]

8.3 Acceptance tests

AT-8.1Save a new script in VS Code: it is listed, with a thumbnail, within 2 s; no restart.
AT-8.2Edit an open figure in VS Code and in the app at once, then save from the app: the conflict is reported, nothing is lost.
AT-8.3Request a path with .., an absolute path, and a foreign origin: all three refused.
AT-8.4Stop the service: the app says so within 5 s; Save is greyed with the reason; start it: Save returns.

9.0 THE SCRIPT HOST AND THE LEGACY ADAPTER

9.1 Isolation

V1 runs scripts in the application's own page, sharing ctx, drawState and window globals; two scripts failed after about a hundred earlier runs (P-12; fixed in V1 by a reset, but structurally still shared). V2 runs each script in its own frame.

DR-9.1Each script shall run in a fresh sandboxed iframe (sandbox="allow-scripts"), with its own canvas, given its settings by message and returning either Geometry (a recorded run) or pixels (a painting script). Nothing it does can reach the application.
DR-9.2A run has a time limit (default 5 s, a setting per script) and a point budget (DR-17.1); past either it is stopped and reported (FR-6.18.2).
DR-9.3An animated script runs only while its view is on screen and stops when left.
DR-9.4The host shall record, while a legacy script runs, every line it draws through the adapter's drawLine and every canvas stroke, giving a recorded geometry that can be placed in a figure as a frozen layer.

9.2 The legacy adapter

The survey of the 185 V1 scripts (R-12) lists what they use: 85 distinct imported names from 29 modules, the drawState fields they touch, bare ctx in 88 scripts, scriptInfo controls with a redrawHandler in 80, armInteractor in 8, draggable points in 3, animation in 4, blending or transparency in 20, fills or text in 29.

DR-9.5Inside the frame, the adapter shall provide every one of those 85 names at the module paths the scripts use (both /draw/x.js and ../../draw/x.js forms), implemented over the V2 kernel where a kernel equivalent exists and as V1's own code otherwise, so every V1 script runs unchanged.
DR-9.6The adapter's scriptInfo support shall build the script's controls in the host's settings panel from its V1 declarations (converted by FR-6.4.8) and call its redrawHandler on change.
DR-9.7Every legacy script shall be classified in a migration ledger: runs, adapted, preview only (fills, text, blending: kept as playpen with their own canvas), or blocked, with a reason.
[[FIG ladder | The ingestion ladder: from a foreign script to a generator]]

9.3 Acceptance tests

AT-9.1Run all 185 legacy scripts in order and shuffled: every one that ran in V1 runs, and its recorded geometry matches V1's approved copy (FR-6.17.4).
AT-9.2A script with an endless loop is stopped at its time limit; the app stays responsive.
AT-9.3A script that writes window.x = 1 leaves no x in the application.

10.0 RENDERING AND OUTPUT

10.1 The canvas renderer

DR-10.1Paint order: background; layers bottom to top (dimmed when not active, unless Show All or Final); discs; weld marks; magic-point and intersection marks (points mode); then, on a separate canvas, handles, selection, centroid and the drag preview.
DR-10.2Final is a renderer option: points only, guides and scaffold left out (FR-6.11.2).
DR-10.3Hit-testing uses the same geometry and transforms the renderer draws, from the evaluation result, never from what was painted.
DR-10.4Device-pixel ratio is honoured, so lines are sharp on high-density screens; line width is in document units, scaled with zoom.

10.2 Physical output

The output is what the owner hammers from. Its correctness is checked with a ruler.

nailsOf(document, evaluation):
  nails = []
  for each disc point (and, if a layer has no discs, each stitch end of a printing layer):
    if the layer's role is guide or scaffold, or includeInOutput is false: skip
    p = its position, in document units, transformed
    add { number: point number, x, y, z, sources: [{ layer, path, i }] }
  merge nails closer than 0.05 mm: one nail, all numbers ("11+12"), all sources   // a weld is already one point
  return nails

templatePages(nails, scale, paper, margin, overlap):
  convert to mm (x * scale); find the extent; tile it with sheets of (paper - 2*margin),
  each overlapping its neighbour by overlap; on each sheet draw every nail inside it (+ the overlap),
  a cross at its centre, its number beside it, alignment marks in the overlap;
  page 1: title, scale, nail size, a 100 mm calibration line and a 10 mm scale bar
DR-10.5The printed 100 mm calibration line shall measure 100 ± 0.5 mm when printed at "actual size"; the cover page says to print at actual size and to measure it.
DR-10.6Nail spacing check: every pair of nails whose centres are closer than diameter + clearance is ringed and listed; it warns, it does not refuse (FR-6.11.6).
DR-10.7Colour cycle (FR-6.11.9, O-14): when on, a nail's colour is palette[step mod 5], step being its index i along its source path; a nail with several sources is drawn as a circle split into its colours. Off by default.
DR-10.8Nail list (CSV): number, x, y, z in the chosen units, sources, merged numbers.
DR-10.9SVG output is the canvas renderer's same paint list written as SVG paths, in mm with a viewBox, so it opens at true size in Inkscape and drives a pen plotter or laser cutter.
DR-10.10Per-layer output (FR-6.11.10): one file per printing layer, the same sheet layout and alignment marks on each, for layers mounted at depth.

10.3 Acceptance tests

AT-10.1Print the calibration page at actual size on the owner's printer; the line measures 100 mm.
AT-10.2A figure 600 mm wide on Letter paper with 10 mm margins and overlap tiles to the expected sheet count; every nail appears on exactly the sheets whose area (with overlap) contains it.
AT-10.3Two welded discs print as one nail with both numbers; two unwelded discs 0.01 mm apart likewise, with a note.
AT-10.4The SVG of a 100 mm square opens in Inkscape measuring 100 mm.
